title: Reading ER Diagrams
summary: Learn to read an entity-relationship diagram: boxes for entity types, ovals for attributes with underlined primary keys, and marked relationship lines showing cardinality and connectivity.

steps.title: Boxes, ovals, and relationship lines
steps.lede: An entity-relationship diagram gives you a map of a schema — every entity, every attribute, and every relationship at a glance.

blocks.text: In an entity-relationship diagram (ERD), an entity type is represented by its name inside a box — Customer, Order, Product, and Order_Item would each get their own box. Each attribute is represented by an oval with its name inside, attached to its entity's box. The primary key attribute is shown by underlining it — customer_id, underlined, inside an oval attached to the Customer box.

An ERD shows relationships between entities as lines: one-to-one (1:1), one-to-many (1:M), and many-to-many (M:N). The Customer-to-Order line would be drawn as 1:M, matching that pair. Markings on a relationship line show cardinality and connectivity — the minimum and maximum number of related entities on each side. A three-pronged symbol means 'many'; a zero and one together mean 'zero or one'; a one-and-only-one symbol means that side is mandatory.

blocks.title: QuickShip ER diagram — customers, orders, products, order_items
blocks.alt_text: ERD with four entity boxes: Customer (customer_id underlined as PK, name, city), Order (order_id underlined as PK, customer_id FK, delivery_minutes), Order_Item (order_id FK+PK, product_id FK+PK), Product (product_id underlined as PK, name). Customer-to-Order line marked 1:M; Order-to-Order_Item marked 1:M; Product-to-Order_Item marked 1:M.

steps.title: Reading an ER diagram
steps.lede: Watch how boxes, ovals, and relationship lines combine to describe the shape of a relational schema.

segments.label: Entity type, instance and set, and the rectangle used to draw an entity
segments.summary: Names the building blocks of an ER model as entities, attributes and relationships. It then uses a student table with roll number as the key to separate an entity type, an individual instance and the set of instances, and closes by saying an entity type is drawn as a rectangular box labelled with the table name.

bridge.before: Watch only for the entity box: an entity type is drawn as a rectangle named after the table.
bridge.after: This range covers just the entity box. How attributes, keys, relationship lines and cardinality markings are drawn is not shown in it; the text above teaches those.

steps.title: Reading cardinality markings
steps.lede: A relationship line between Customer and Order has a three-pronged symbol on the Order side and a one-and-only-one symbol on the Customer side. What does this mean?

public.prompt: A relationship line between Customer and Order has a three-pronged symbol on the Order side and a one-and-only-one symbol on the Customer side. What does this mean?

options.text: Each customer must have exactly one order, and each order can belong to many customers
Each order must be linked to exactly one customer (mandatory), and one customer can be linked to many orders
Many customers can be linked to many orders
A customer may have zero or one order, and each order belongs to exactly one customer

opt_correct.message: Correct. The one-and-only-one symbol on the Customer side means each order must be linked to exactly one customer (mandatory). The three-pronged symbol on the Order side means one customer can be linked to many orders — a one-to-many relationship.

opt_one_to_many.message: Not quite. The three-pronged symbol is on the Order side, meaning 'many orders' per customer — not 'many customers' per order. The one-and-only-one symbol on the Customer side means each order belongs to exactly one customer.

opt_many_to_many.message: Not quite. A many-to-many relationship would require three-pronged symbols on both sides. Here only the Order side has the three-pronged symbol, making this a one-to-many relationship.

opt_optional.message: Not quite. A 'zero or one' symbol would show a zero and a one together. The one-and-only-one symbol means mandatory — exactly one customer per order, not zero or one.

correct.message: Correct. The three-pronged symbol means 'many' on the Order side; the one-and-only-one symbol means each order must belong to exactly one customer.

incorrect.message: Remember: a three-pronged symbol means 'many'; a one-and-only-one symbol means that side is mandatory (exactly one).

hints: Which side of the line has the three-pronged symbol? That side is the 'many' side.
The one-and-only-one symbol means that side is mandatory — every order must be linked to exactly one customer.

steps.title: Classify ERD elements and read relationships
steps.lede: Given the QuickShip ER diagram, classify each element as an entity, attribute, or primary key, and read each relationship line's cardinality.

public.prompt: The QuickShip ER diagram contains four entity boxes (Customer, Order, Product, Order_Item), attribute ovals, underlined primary keys, and relationship lines. Classify each element below as it would appear in the diagram.

buckets.label: Not an ERD element (data value, not structure)

items.text: customer_id — the oval attached to Customer, with its name underlined
city — the oval attached to Customer, name not underlined
The line between Customer and Order (three-pronged symbol on the Order side)
The line between Order and Product (three-pronged symbols on both sides, resolved via Order_Item)
customer_id = 1 — the integer value stored in the first row of the customers table

item_customer_box.message: Correct. In an ERD, an entity type is represented by its name inside a rectangle — Customer is an entity box.

item_order_box.message: Correct. Order is an entity type, drawn as a rectangle labelled 'Order'.

item_customer_id_oval.message: Correct. customer_id is the primary key attribute of Customer — it is shown as an oval with its name underlined.

item_city_oval.message: Correct. city is a regular attribute of Customer — shown as an oval without underlining, since it is not the primary key.

item_customer_order_line.message: Correct. The three-pronged symbol on the Order side means 'many orders per customer' — a one-to-many relationship line.

item_order_product_line.message: Correct. Three-pronged symbols on both sides indicate a many-to-many relationship between Order and Product (resolved in the schema by the Order_Item junction table).

item_order_item_box.message: Correct. Order_Item is an entity type (the junction/composite entity), drawn as a rectangle in the ERD.

item_trap_customer_id_number.message: Correct. This is a data value (the integer 1 stored in a row), not an ERD element. In an ERD, customer_id appears as an underlined oval (a primary key attribute), not as a row value. The ERD shows structure, not data.

correct.message: Excellent. You correctly identified entities, attributes, primary keys, and relationship types — and recognised that a data value is not an ERD element.

incorrect.message: Review the ERD notation: rectangles are entities, ovals are attributes, underlined ovals are primary keys, and lines with cardinality markings show relationships.

hints: In an ERD, shapes matter: rectangles are entities, ovals are attributes. Is the item a shape in the diagram or a value in a table row?
For relationship lines, count the prongs: one prong on each side means one-to-one; three prongs on one side means one-to-many; three prongs on both sides means many-to-many.

steps.title: What you've learned
steps.lede: One diagram type that maps an entire relational schema.

blocks.text: In an ERD, each entity type is a box, each attribute is an oval attached to its box, and the primary key attribute is underlined. Relationship lines show cardinality: a three-pronged symbol means 'many', a one-and-only-one symbol means mandatory, and a zero-and-one symbol means optional. Reading those markings tells you the minimum and maximum number of related entities on each side of every relationship.

blocks.title: Up next: Joining Tables in SQL
blocks.text: In the next tile you'll use the relationships you've just mapped to write SQL JOIN queries — combining rows from two tables using the foreign key links the ER diagram describes.

remediation_steps.title: Cardinality markings: a clear contrast
remediation_steps.lede: Two relationship lines — one mandatory one-to-many, one optional.

blocks.text: Line A: Customer — Order, with a one-and-only-one symbol on the Customer side and a three-pronged symbol on the Order side. Reading: each order belongs to exactly one customer (mandatory), and one customer can have many orders. Line B: Customer — Order, with a zero-and-one symbol on the Customer side and a three-pronged symbol on the Order side. Reading: each order may belong to zero or one customer (optional). The symbol on each side tells you the minimum and maximum for that side — not the other.
